meta.title: Operation of Rotary Vacuum Evaporator in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To efficiently concentrate or completely evaporate organic solvents from crude plant extracts under reduced pressure and controlled temperature, preserving heat-sensitive phytochemicals during solvent removal.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for concentration of alcoholic, hydroalcoholic, and other solvent extracts from Soxhlet extraction, maceration, or percolation processes.
procedure: Ensure the water bath is filled with distilled water and set to the required temperature: 40°C for methanol/ethanol extracts; 30–35°C for ether or highly volatile solvents; maximum 60°C for aqueous extracts.
Check that the condenser is connected to the cold water supply (5–15°C) and water is flowing before starting.
Connect the vacuum pump to the rotary evaporator via the cold trap; ensure the cold trap is filled with ice or dry ice/acetone mixture.
Attach the receiving flask (500 mL or 1 L) to the outlet port — use a Keck clip to secure.
Pour the plant extract (max 2/3 volume of the evaporating flask) into the evaporating flask.
Attach the evaporating flask to the rotary joint using a Keck clip — ensure it is secure.
Lower the evaporating flask into the water bath.
Set the rotation speed: typically 40–80 RPM — rotation ensures even heating and increases evaporation surface area.
Apply vacuum gradually: open the vacuum valve slowly; target vacuum 50–200 mbar depending on solvent.
Switch on the rotation motor — the flask should rotate smoothly.
Monitor distillate collection in the receiving flask; periodically empty the receiving flask if it fills.
Continue until no more solvent drips into the receiving flask.
To stop: first turn off the vacuum pump; slowly open the bleed valve to restore atmospheric pressure; stop rotation; raise flask out of water bath.
Remove the evaporating flask and transfer the concentrate to a tared container.
Record: solvent, volume, bath temperature, vacuum, and final extract weight/volume in the logbook.
precautions: Never apply vacuum to a warm, sealed, or glued joint — sudden pressure drop can cause implosion.
Always use round-bottom flasks — flat-bottomed flasks implode under vacuum.
Ensure all glass joints and connections are intact — cracked glassware is an implosion hazard under vacuum.
Always release vacuum slowly using the bleed valve before stopping the pump.
Keep the cold trap filled — solvent vapours entering the vacuum pump destroy the pump oil.
Do not heat above 60°C — most phytochemicals begin to degrade above this temperature.
Use appropriate bump protection (boiling chips) for bumping-prone extracts.
Wear goggles — glassware under vacuum can shatter unexpectedly.
